newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BAGGIO SET TO GO TO BOLOGNA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAGGIO SET TO GO TO BOLOGNA.

text.p: Italy midfielder Roberto Baggio looks set to move to serie A side Bologna next season after an agreement was reached with AC Milan, Italian newspapers said on Wednesday.
"Milan and Bologna have reached an agreement to bring Baggio to the "Red and Blues" (Bologna)," club president Giuseppe Frascara was quoted as saying by La Gazzetta dello Sport.
Frascara said Baggio would make an announcement on his decision at 1100 GMT at a meeting to present Milan's squad for next season.
"Now its up to the player," Frascara said.

News reports on Wednesday speculated over the terms of the deal for Baggio, who was once the world's most expensive player but spent most of last season on the bench at Milan and lost his regular national spot.
La Gazzetta said the deal would earn Milan 4.8 billion lire ($2.8 million) over the two-year contract, with Baggio drawing a yearly salary of at least 2.5 billion lire ($1.5 million).
According to the reports, Baggio would be free to leave after only one season if he wished.

There was no comment from the 30-year-old attacking midfielder. Milan vice-president Adriano Galliani said the club had received other offers for Baggio and would give the player the freedom to decide his future.
"We have given Baggio complete freedom of choice. As well as Bologna, we have had offers, slightly less tempting, from Udinese, Derby County and Borussia Dortmund," Galliani said.

Galliani said on Tuesday Milan had received two offers for Baggio from English clubs but did not elaborate. The player has also been linked to Spain's Barcelona and Atletico Madrid as well as a number of top Italian sides.
